answer: Let attestations define a weighted graph, and propagate trust by a length-bounded random walk so distant influence decays rather than accumulating unchecked. A sybil cluster may echo internally, but a sparse external boundary gives it low conductance—the cut weight divided by cluster volume—and thus low escape probability per step. With an honest anchor and bounded walk horizon, min-cut and transitivity bounds limit the cluster’s aggregate voting weight, even when members spiral into dense mutual endorsements.
